# Supplemental runtime license evidence

Evidence date: **2026-11-05**. These upstream files retain **their own copyright notices and terms**. The project's Apache license does not relicense this material.

`catalog.json` maps the exact published NuGet IDs/versions to their declared licensing metadata, fixed repository commits, public source URLs and retained file hashes. This directory supplements the runtime collector's byte-exact **NuGet-embedded** notices; these files came separately from identified upstream repositories and a vendor release archive. Do not describe them as embedded NuGet files or automatically clear the collector's review flags. The catalog's `researchInventoryAnchor` identifies the historical research input, **not a final package inventory binding**. A final package must independently match each listed package ID/version, nuspec/repository evidence and raw archive digest; its component-manifest hashes or full inventory hash may differ.

The six `upstream/` license files come from repository commits recorded in the exact package nuspecs. One Microsoft license covers both `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` and `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core`. The PDFium build-repository license is separate from the native library/component notices; it is not a blanket native grant. The complete fixed-commit PdfPig license file includes its external-component notices and is retained without truncation.

`pdfium-152.0.7961-osx-arm64/` preserves **16 vendor license/notice files plus VERSION** from the [immutable PDFium release](https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases/tag/chromium%2F7961). The release tag resolves to the exact commit recorded in the NuGet package. The archive's SHA-256 matches its published asset digest, and its native library's SHA-256 exactly matches the osx-arm64 member of `bblanchon.PDFium.macOS/152.0.7961`. The native library was hashed directly from the archives; **no binary was copied here or executed**. The catalog retains the URLs, asset ID, hashes and member paths.

There is a licensing-metadata distinction to review: that NuGet package declares Apache-2.0, while the exact vendor archive contains an MIT build-package license, a BSD-style PDFium license and separate bundled-component notices. Preserve all of them; do not assume a single SPDX field overrides the other material.

Four exact-version gaps remain: `SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3`, `SQLitePCLRaw.core`, `SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3` and `SQLitePCLRaw.provider.e_sqlite3`, all **2.1.13**. Their nuspecs declare Apache-2.0 but omit a source commit, and neither checked 2.1.13 tag form was available. No adjacent-version license has been substituted and labelled exact. Their existing nuspec copyright/author/declared-license evidence remains available in the runtime inventory.

This is **not legal redistribution approval, signature verification or a complete native SBOM**. Those fields remain false in the catalog. Source-to-binary reproducibility, every native component/RID, framework/runtime and development-toolchain notices, and dataset/model rights require separate review. No dependency, binary or upstream code was adopted by adding this evidence; packaging performs no network retrieval for it.
